risks: Our business operations are primarily engaged in the manufacture and supply of sulphur-based inorganic chemicals, which have critical applications in the food and beverages, oil drilling and chemical industries.
The chemical industry, being diverse and competitive, is subject to volatility in raw material prices, energy costs, technological shifts, and global trade

We have not faced any such instances in the past, however, any adverse developments in one or more of these sectors, such as a downturn in demand, regulatory tightening, commodity price fluctuations, or increased competition, may lead to a decline in demand for our products.
Moreover, customers may shift to lower-priced alternatives or substitutes, which could adversely affect our pricing, margins, and overall financial performance.
Our Company derives revenue from diversified customers.

Our inability to acquire new customers or loss of all or a substantial portion of any of our major customers, for any reason and/or continued reduction of the business from them, could have a material adverse impact on our business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.
Our Company derives revenues from diversified customers.

We cannot assure that we will be able to maintain historic levels of business from our top one (1), five (5) and ten (10) customers, or that we will be able to reduce customer concentration in the future.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Red Herring Prospectus does not describe any backward- or forward-integration programme for the Company itself. Its primary raw materials - sulphur dioxide, sodium hydroxide and sodium carbonate (with anhydrous ammonia, soda ash light, caustic soda flakes and caustic lye also material) - are bought from a diversified third-party supplier base located in India, and the Company states it has not entered into any long-term supply arrangement or agreement with its suppliers. The DRHP frames its sourcing advantage as locational rather than integrated: the manufacturing units are described as strategically located in close proximity to industries that generate liquified sulphur dioxide, which the Company says gives consistent and reliable sources of key raw materials and reduces logistics cost and lead time. The Company moved in the opposite direction on upstream processing in Fiscal 2019, when it transitioned from using sulphur burning furnaces to procuring liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2), which it states improved production efficiency, reduced emissions and enhanced environmental compliance. For Phase II of Manufacturing Unit - II the Company proposes to install a sulphur burner system with a waste heat boiler that will generate fuel-free steam for plant operations without relying on external fuel sources - an in-house utility rather than product capacity. Downstream, the Company sells business-to-business directly through its own India-based sales and marketing team and states that it currently does not have any sales and distribution network for its domestic and export customers; it intends to build a distribution network in Europe, North America and South America. It has not entered into any technical or other collaboration or joint venture agreement, and it uses third-party logistics for both inbound raw materials and outbound finished goods, with no long-term contracts with any logistics service provider. Trading of bought-out goods (soda ash dense, Ecosoft, high carbon ferro chrome and similar lines) sits alongside manufacturing in revenue from operations.

overview.business_model: The Company manufactures and supplies sulphur-based inorganic chemicals from two owned units in Gujarat and sells them to industrial customers across food and beverages, chemicals, oil drilling, pharmaceuticals, ceramics, agrochemicals, water treatment, petrochemicals, cosmetics, paints, polymers, boilers and mining, in both food grade and technical grade purity levels. Products are used as preservatives, reducing agents, oxygen scavengers, dechlorinating agents, bleaching agents and process intermediates. Revenue is earned on product sales in the domestic market and on exports (the RHP states domestic sales constituted 70.72% for the two-month period ended May 31, 2026); the RHP also discloses a trading component alongside manufacturing. Manufacturing Unit - I at Vatva has an installed capacity of 18,800 MTPA; Phase I of Manufacturing Unit - II at Bavla (18,000 MTPA) commenced commercial production with effect from February 2025, taking combined installed capacity to 36,800 MTPA; Phase II at Bavla is proposed at 78,544 MTPA. Since Fiscal 2019 the Company procures liquefied sulphur dioxide (SO2) rather than using sulphur burning furnaces, and its units are stated to be located close to industries that generate liquefied SO2. Stated revenue from operations grew from Rs 4,486.72 lakhs in Fiscal 2024 to Rs 7,122.02 lakhs in Fiscal 2026, with EBITDA of Rs 1,539.72 lakhs and PAT of Rs 1,022.00 lakhs in Fiscal 2026 (all figures Rs in lakhs, as stated in the RHP).

litigation_summary.materiality_threshold_basis: Materiality Policy approved by Board resolution dated September 04, 2025, with the threshold determined per the Audited Financial Statements and approved by board resolution dated July 18, 2026. A matter is material if the monetary amount of the claim made by or against the Company, its subsidiary, Promoters or Directors is equal to or in excess of the LOWEST of: (i) 2% of turnover per the last audited financial statements, amounting to ₹142.44 lakhs; (ii) 2% of net worth per the last audited financial statements, amounting to ₹96.64 lakhs; or (iii) 5% of the average absolute value of profit or loss after tax per the last three audited financial statements, amounting to ₹39.59 lakhs. The lowest of the three, ₹39.59 lakhs, is the operative threshold. Two further limbs apply regardless of amount: (b) where the decision in one case is likely to affect the decision in similar cases and the aggregate of such cases exceeds the clause (a) amount; and (c) any litigation not meeting clause (a) an adverse outcome in which would materially and adversely affect the operations or financial position of the Company. Pre-litigation notices from third parties (other than show cause notices from statutory, regulatory or tax authorities, notices threatening criminal action, or first information reports) are not treated as material litigation until the relevant party is impleaded as a defendant before a judicial or arbitral forum.
